learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with basic knowledge about the different heat transfer mechanisms.
Study and design of heat exchange equipment (heat exchangers).
Refrigeration and air conditioning production focusing specifically on vapor compression cycles with phase change as they are the most used in the industry.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Concepts of heat transfer by convection
Vapor compression refrigeration machines. HVAC / Industrial Refrigeration installations.
Absorption refrigeration machines. HVAC / Industrial Refrigeration installations.
Basic elements of Heating and Domestic Hot Water (DHW) installations.
Sizing of radiators, boilers, underfloor heating, pipes, and insulation.
Particular case of DHW production by Solar Thermal Energy.
teaching_methods: Group work (preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects)

assessment_methods.method: Reports and results of practical execution tests

assessment_rules: For the first call, evaluation consists of three partial exams (26.25%, 26.25%, 11.25%), practical work (11.25%), and an integrated project (25%). The average of the partial exams, before considering the integrated project, must be at least 3.5 points. A total final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. If the Integrated Project is not completed, a minimum grade of 4 in the first two partials is required to average with the rest of the components. For the second call, students can choose to keep the Integrated Project grade (25%) and take an exam worth 75%, or take a 100% exam if they do not keep the project grade. Partial grades from the first call may be kept and averaged; if not averaging with the PI, a minimum of 4 in the partials is required to average.
bibliography: Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer (Dewit, David P; Incropera, Frank P.;Bergman, Theodore L.; Lavine, Adrienne S.)
